what: Market chance adjusted by recent shots, shots on target, goal difference and form. For each outcome: logit(chance) = logit(bookmaker average, margin removed) + z · coef, then the three chances are scaled to add up to 1. z are the four inputs standardised with the mean and sd below. A second, separate view comes from Elo ratings: when Elo rates a side no higher than the market does, the market has seen something Elo has not, and the shots edge on that side holds up better.

inputs.sotd: (home side's shots on target for − against, average of its last 8 league matches) − the same for the away side
inputs.form: home side's points in its last 5 league matches − the away side's

trained_on: Top five leagues, 2006/07 to 2016/17 seasons, about 19,000 matches with bookmaker averages and shot counts.
checked_on: The seasons after that, not used for fitting.

R.what: Our xG model with home advantage (the fair-odds pages) sees an edge of at least 10% on the away side against the average price, and the home price is below 4.00: bet the home side. That model rates home sides too low this season, so its away 'edges' have pointed the wrong way.
R.found_text: Found on this season's matches up to 2 November: 54 bets, +14.8 units (+27.3%), up in all five leagues. It has not been checked on any other season, so treat it as a test.

elo.what: elofootball.com's published method: home win expectancy 1 / (10^(−d/400) + 1) with d = home rating + 100 − away rating; after the match each side moves by k × goal-difference factor × (result − expectancy), result 1 / 0.5 / 0. Goal-difference factor 1 for a margin of 0 or 1, 1.5 for 2, (11 + margin) / 8 for more. A promoted club that never played in the league starts at the average of the clubs relegated the season before; a returning club keeps its old rating. League matches only.

fit.what: Elo difference → chance, fitted on the same older seasons: logit(chance) = a + b·x + c·x², x = d / 100. The draw is what is left (at least 5%), then the three are scaled to add up to 1.
